ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as most recently amended by Act No. 19930, effective 2024) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 14782, as amended); Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Act No. 5493, as amended); Financial Services Commission Regulation on Financial Transaction Information Reporting and Usage; Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) AML/CFT Guidance on Beneficial Owner Identification and Enhanced Due Diligence for High-Risk Commodity Sectors; Commercial Act Article 287-2 and the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act regarding corporate registration and member disclosure.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Company Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry Office, Supreme Court of Korea Registry Administration (Internet Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certificate is issued by the Korean court registry. If the destination state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, the court-certified instrument receives an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA); no consular step is added. If the destination state is not a Hague member, the instrument is legalized by the Korean MOFA and then by the destination Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; they are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Current Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean District Court Registry Office of the registered Yuhan Hoesa seat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The registry extract is certified by the issuing court registry. For Apostille Convention destinations, MOFA affixes the Apostille to the certified extract. For non-convention destinations, MOFA authentication is followed by consular legalization at the destination embassy in Korea. The two authentication routes are separate and mutually exclusive; neither path is applied after the other when one has already been completed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney and Board Resolution for Pre-Incorporation and Registration Filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prospective incorporators and designated directors, witnessed by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: After signature before a Korean notary public, the notarial certificate is submitted either to the Korean MOFA for an Apostille if the destination country is an Apostille contracting state, or to the Korean MOFA and the destination consulate for consular legalization if the destination country is not a contracting state. The two methods are parallel and mutually exclusive; consular legalization is never added after an Apostille and an Apostille is never added after consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators of the Yuhan Hoesa, adopted in an Incorporators Meeting and notarized where the incorporators elect the non-subscription incorporation procedure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The articles are signed and date-stamped by incorporators and, where required, notarized. The authentic document is then apostilled by MOFA for Apostille Convention states or legalized by MOFA and the destination consulate for non-member states. The apostille route and the consular legalization route are applied in the alternative, never in combination.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Relationship Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank, signed by the branch relationship manager and bank compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter is issued on bank letterhead with an attested signature. The signature is notarized and the notarized letter is either submitted to MOFA for Apostille for Hague member states, or submitted to MOFA and the destination consulate for consular legalization for non-member states. The two routes are mutually exclusive and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Source of Wealth Statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owners and directors, witnessed by a Korean licensed attorney or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The declaration is signed by each UBO before a notary or attorney, and the notarial/attorney certification is then processed either through MOFA Apostille for Apostille Convention destinations or through MOFA plus destination consular legalization for non-convention destinations. Apostille and consular legalization are separate parallel procedures and are not combined in a single chain.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs, authorized signatories, counterparties, freighters, and supply-chain intermediaries against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) watch list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the United States OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs designated-terrorist list, the European Union consolidated sanctions list, and the FATF public statements for high-risk jurisdictions. Each natural person and legal entity must be screened before onboarding, then re-screened every 30 days and upon any trigger event. A minimum scorecard must include name transliteration variants, date of birth, passport or corporate registration number, and country of residence. PEP identification requires enhanced due diligence, independent source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence for each transaction, senior management approval for the opening of the Yuhan Hoesa corporate account, heightened monitoring of Swift wires and standby LC payment rails, and a 5-year retention of all AML records.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr, together with the Korea Trade and Trademark Office name-search service for corporate trademark clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the legal name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be registered in Hangul and must include the statutory entity suffix Yuhan Hoesa. A separate English transliteration may be recorded on the registration file as the English trade name, but it does not replace the Hangul corporate name. The statutory four-tier naming doctrine in practice requires the following order: first, the entity-type suffix Yuhan Hoesa; second, a distinctive core trade name that distinguishes the entity from existing registered companies; third, an optional industry or class descriptor; and fourth, an optional branch or representative-office marker. If any element is romanized into a foreign language, the romanization must be a direct phonetic transliteration approved by the registry and must be disclosed consistently in all banking and licensing documents. The name-search must cover identical and confusingly similar Hangul strings, including homophones and names that use alternative Hanja readings, because the Korean registry rejects names that are dangerously similar to an existing company in the same business sector.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must file a formal written objection with the competent district court registry office within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice. The objection must cite the exact refusal ground, the relevant articles of the Korean Commercial Act, and must propose two to three alternative Hangul name variants that remove the conflicting token. The applicant should attach the preliminary license approval for petroleum wholesale brokerage and evidence of fee payment. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative review with the head of the Supreme Court Registry Administration under the Administrative Litigation Act, and thereafter may institute an administrative suit in the competent district court within 30 days from notice of the adverse review. Counsel should verify the competing company name and rescission deadlines before every refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected as the primary registered office for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in ISIC 4661 wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates. The National Tax Service, the Korean Customs Service, and licensed banks require a physical place of business where the corporate books, contracts, bills of lading, shipment records, and AML/CFT files can be inspected. Korean banking counterparties will reject a client that maintains only a virtual office for an energy-commodity trading entity, and the petroleum special licensing authorities require actual commercial substance such as leased office space, staff presence, and local bank account operations. A virtual mailing address may be used only as an auxiliary correspondence address and must never appear as the statutory registered office on the corporate registration or tax certificate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) municipal local tax office verification visit; (2) Korean Customs Service unannounced trade-compliance inspection; (3) petroleum business license audit by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or delegated Korea Petroleum Association; (4) bank on-site due diligence visit before account activation; and (5) Korea Coast Guard and FIU special-license review for marine fuel operators. The quantified risk is high: there is an approximate 70-85% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of registration, with the probability increasing to 80-85% if the entity is classified as a high-risk energy commodity trader using Swift wire and standby letter of credit payment rails. Official notice of inspection can be as short as 1 to 10 business days, and the Yuhan Hoesa must maintain full records, original registry documents, lease agreements, payroll evidence, and tax filings at the physical registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000 of 1962, as comprehensively amended), notably Articles 169 (juridical capacity and existence of company), 287 (promoter duties), 289 (contents of articles of incorporation), 290 (certification of articles of incorporation), 312 (place and effect of registration), 317 (effective date of incorporation), 330 (nullity of incorporation), 331 (liability of promoters), 543-589 (limited liability company, Yuhan Hoesa), Article 544 (certificate of contribution quota), Article 547 (corporate governance of limited liability company), Article 560 (auditor), and Article 562 (dissolution restrictions), together with the Supreme Court Regulations on Registration of Commercial Entities and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for inbound capital investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office (Beobwonsa) of the Seoul Central District Court or the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, administered through the Supreme Court's Internet Registration System (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Liability Company Establishment Registration Application (Application for Registration of Establishment of Yuhan Hoesa), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the certificate of capital contribution deposit, all filed with the competent district court registration office under Commercial Act Article 317 and the Registration of Commercial Establishments Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) under the Commercial Act; the incorporators are free to fix paid-in capital at any amount in the articles of incorporation. There is no mandatory blocked escrow account under general company law. However, before filing the establishment registration, the full amount of cash capital contributions must be deposited into a domestic Korean bank account opened in the name of the promoter or prospective company, and a bank-issued certificate of capital deposit must be obtained and submitted to the registration court. Non-cash contributions must be inspected and valued by a notarized valuation report with the consent of the incorporators. For foreign investors, the capital subscription and remittance must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and a Foreign Investment Report Certificate may be required. Although company law prescribes no minimum capital, the petroleum wholesale license under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act may impose separate financial capacity requirements, solvency thresholds, or storage facility commitments based on the annual trading volume.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) ADOPTED AT THE ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING HELD ON [DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE]. At a duly convened meeting of the incorporators acting as the first board of directors of the Company, the chair confirmed that due notice had been given or waived by all persons entitled to attend and vote, that a quorum was present in accordance with the articles of incorporation, and that all attendees unanimously agreed to adopt the following resolutions. FIRST: SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The capital subscription schedule attached as Exhibit A is approved in full. The paid-in capital of the Company is hereby fixed at the amount set forth in the articles of incorporation, and the subscribers named in the subscription schedule are deemed to have validly subscribed to their respective contribution quotas. The chief executive officer is directed to demand, receive, and collect all unpaid capital contributions and to deposit all such funds into a domestic bank account standing in the name of the Company before the corporate registration application is submitted to the competent court. No share capital may be repaid or reduced except in compliance with the Commercial Act and a subsequent board or general meeting resolution. SECOND: BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The board designates the initial Korean bank identified in Exhibit B as the Company's principal depositary. The board authorizes the opening of corporate accounts, including operating accounts, payroll accounts, and trade finance accounts, in the name of the Company. All withdrawals, bank guarantees, letters of credit, and deposit transactions shall require the joint signature of the chief executive officer and one other director, or the single signature of the chief executive officer under the corporate seal, in accordance with the banking mandate executed with the financial institution. The authorized officers shall comply with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Real Name Financial Transactions Act, and all anti-money laundering obligations and directives of the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. THIRD: REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is hereby adopted as the address specified in the articles of incorporation and shall be the place where the corporate register, books of account, minutes, and records of the Company are maintained. All legal processes, statutory notices, and demands may be served at that address during ordinary business hours. The chief executive officer is authorized to execute and deliver any lease, sublease, utility contract, and address change filing required by the registry, the tax authority, and the municipal government. FOURTH: STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The board hereby appoints the following persons as statutory officers of the Company: (i) as representative chief executive officer, the person named in the articles of incorporation; (ii) as director, the person named in the articles of incorporation; and (iii) as auditor or statutory auditor, the person or external audit firm named in the articles of incorporation, if required by law. The representative chief executive officer is for all purposes the statutory representative of the Company and is granted plenary authority to execute all registration filings, tax returns, license applications, contracts, and legal instruments necessary for the conduct of the Company's business. FIFTH: FURTHER AUTHORIZATIONS. The board authorizes and directs management to prepare, execute, and file all documents required to obtain the business registration certificate, the petroleum wholesale registration, and any environmental, civil defense, fire safety, and occupational safety permits necessary for the physical wholesale brokerage of crude oil and refined petroleum products. Management is also authorized to engage local counsel, accountants, and notaries as required, and to take all lawful actions necessary to carry out this resolution. This resolution is final, immediately effective, and shall continue in full force and effect until lawfully amended or rescinded. CERTIFIED this [DATE]. Chairman of the First Board of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Capital Deposit Escrow Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Online Registration System (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr and the selected licensed commercial bank in Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name-availability search on the Supreme Court Online Registration System (IROS) to confirm that the proposed Korean corporate name 'Yuhan Hoesa' does not conflict with any existing registered trade name. In parallel, open a temporary subscription deposit account at a Korean licensed bank in the name of the promoter or the prospective company, and deposit the agreed paid-in capital. Obtain an official bank-issued certificate of capital deposit stating the depositor, account number, deposit amount, and date. Draft the articles of incorporation covering the corporate name, business purpose, registered office, paid-in capital, contribution quotas, number of directors and auditor, fiscal year, meeting procedures, publication method, and liquidation provisions. Have all incorporators execute the draft articles and passport copies, and for any foreign incorporator, obtain and notarize a power of attorney in favor of the local formation agent.
required_dossiers: Proposed Korean company name and IROS name search result printout
Draft articles of incorporation signed by all incorporators
Passport or national identity document of each incorporator
Alien registration card or foreign investment report certificate for non-resident incorporators, if applicable
Bank certificate of capital contribution deposit
Power of attorney for the local formation agent and notarized identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IROS identifies a conflicting corporate name, select an alternative name and repeat the search until a valid name is available. If the bank refuses to open the deposit account due to incomplete foreign investor documentation, provide the missing notarized identity evidence or amend the account title to a qualified Korean resident agent. Any discrepancy in the deposit certificate must be cured by obtaining a corrected certificate from the bank before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Subscription Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public engaged under the Korean Notary Association or a notary at the nearest Korean consulate for documents executed abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the fully executed draft articles of incorporation and related subscription instruments to a Korean notary public for notarization under Commercial Act Article 290. The notary will verify the identity and legal capacity of each incorporator, confirm that the incorporators understand the contents of the articles, witness their signatures, and certify the document as the authentic and binding starting-point of the company. If any incorporator or officer is located outside Korea, the power of attorney and execution pages must be notarized locally, consularized or apostilled, and accompanied by a Korean translation. The notary will annotate each corrected page and execute the notarial certificate. After notarization, no substantive amendment may be made to the articles without preparing and executing a corrected version and repeating the notarization process.
required_dossiers: Signed draft articles of incorporation in Korean or bilingual form
Subscription schedule identifying each subscriber and quota amount
Certificate of capital contribution deposit from the bank
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney for each non-resident incorporator or officer
Passport copies and Korean alien registration cards, if applicable
Company formation instruction letter and officer consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to the articles due to substantive illegality or missing signature, revise the affected clauses and have all incorporators re-execute the document before seeking notarization again. If a foreign signature lacks apostille or consular authentication, obtain the required legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate and resubmit the document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registration Office of the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, or the online IROS filing portal accepted by the Supreme Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of establishment of the Yuhan Hoesa with the competent court registration office, either in person or through IROS, within the statutory period after the organizational meeting. Submit the notarized articles of incorporation, the bank-issued certificate of capital contribution deposit, the officer acceptance declarations, the corporate seal registration data, and the written consent of each officer. Pay the court registration tax and education surcharge at the prescribed rate and obtain the official receipt. The registrar will examine whether the company name is lawful, whether paid-in capital has been fully deposited, whether the registered office lies within the court's territorial jurisdiction, and whether the articles and officers comply with the Commercial Act. Upon successful review, the court enters the company in the commercial register and issues a certified registry extract, which is conclusive evidence of incorporation. The company exists as a separate legal entity from the moment of such registration.
required_dossiers: Registration application form for establishment of a limited liability company
Notarized articles of incorporation
Certificate of capital contribution deposit
Bank receipt of paid-in capital deposit
Written consent and acceptance forms of each representative officer, director, and auditor
Corporate seal registration card and seal specimen
Power of attorney for the agent filing the registration
Official receipt of registration tax and education surcharge payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a deficiency notice or suspends registration, cure the stated defect within the granted supplementary period and refile through IROS. If the court rejects the application, request a written rejection decision and pursue an administrative appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act. Common cures include correcting the address of the registered office, submitting a corrected capital deposit certificate, or replacing a non-compliant officer consent form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the Hometax portal or the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the business registration certificate within sixty days after the court registration date. The application shall contain the corporate identification number, corporate name, taxable business type, ISIC business code 4661 for wholesale of solid, liquid and gaseous fuels and related products, the registered office address, and the name of the chief executive officer. Attach the certified corporate registry extract, notarized articles of incorporation, corporate seal registration certificate, registered office lease agreement or proof of ownership, and the representative officer's identification. The NTS will assign a unique business registration number, register the company for corporate income tax, value-added tax, payroll tax, and local withholding obligations, and issue the official business registration certificate. This certificate is a precondition for opening permanent corporate bank accounts, importing goods, and applying for industrial operating permits.
required_dossiers: Official application for business registration (NTS Form)
Certified copy of corporate registry extract (court register)
Notarized articles of incorporation
Corporate seal registration certificate
Registered office lease agreement or title document
Photocopy of representative officer's ID card or alien registration card
Power of attorney for tax agency representation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries any information on the application, respond in writing through Hometax or the district tax office and supply correcting documentation. If the business registration certificate is withheld because the registered office lease is invalid, submit a valid lease or a registered office consent letter from the landlord. If delayed, the company may ask for a certificate of non-assessment showing the tax representative and pending items.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Petroleum Wholesale Operating License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Government (Si/Gun/Gu) head delegated by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), with post-registration recording at Korea National Oil Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for petroleum sales business registration (wholesale) under Article 5 of the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act. The application shall describe the company's business scope as the physical wholesale brokerage and trading of crude oil and refined petroleum products, including marine fuel oil and distillates, and shall demonstrate statutory qualification, financial capacity, business site or facility compliance, storage or handling arrangements, safety management plan, and zoning compatibility. The local government may inspect the registered office and, if storage tanks exist, require proof of compliance with the Firefighting Facilities Installation and Maintenance Act, environmental impact assessment permits, and the Hazardous Chemicals Management Act. Upon approval, the authority issues the Petroleum Sales Business (Wholesale) Registration Certificate, and the company must be recorded in the Korea National Oil Corporation trader registry. The certificate must be retained at the registered office, renewed annually as prescribed, and amended within thirty days of any material change in officers, capital, address, or storage facilities.
required_dossiers: Petroleum Sales Business Registration (Wholesale) application form
Business registration certificate from NTS
Certified corporate registry extract
Notarized articles of incorporation
Chief executive officer identification and seal certificate
Proof of financial capacity, including bank statements or audited financial statements
Site and facility drawings, if storage or handling facilities are operated
Fire safety certificate and civil defense inspection records, if applicable
Environmental impact assessment approval or exemption confirmation, if applicable
Power of attorney for the authorized license agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local government rejects or suspends the application, the company may request a written statement of reasons and file an administrative appeal with the provincial administrative appeals commission or initiate administrative litigation. Typical remedies include providing additional financial documentation, revising the site plan, obtaining missing fire or environmental permits, or appointing a qualified storage or handling contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the delegated competent Si/Gun/Gu municipal government, in coordination with the Korea National Oil Corporation for the petroleum trader registry and the Korea Gas Safety Corporation for facility safety, if applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Petroleum Sales Business Registration (Wholesale) under Article 5 of the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act, issued by the competent local government head.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) and the Korea Environment Corporation (K-Eco) Environmental Impact Assessment Center
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a Full Environmental Impact Assessment for the pure physical wholesale brokerage and trading of crude oil and refined petroleum products, provided the company does not construct, expand, or operate fixed petroleum storage tanks or transfer facilities. If the company installs crude oil or refined product storage tanks, loading arms, or cargo transfer equipment, the project will be classified under the Prior Environmental Review System or Full Environmental Impact Assessment category under Articles 22 and 43 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act depending on the total storage capacity and annual petroleum throughput.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any permitted storage or transfer facility, quantitative compliance is mandated under the Clean Air Conservation Act, the Water Environment Conservation Act, the Wastes Control Act, and the Hazardous Chemicals Management Act. Marine loading and storage operations must achieve a volatile organic compound (VOC) vapor recovery efficiency of at least ninety-five percent where vapor balancing or recovery systems are installed. Effluent discharged to public waters or sewerage systems must meet the applicable industrial effluent standards, including BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 40 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 5 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 60 mg/L, and total phosphorus not exceeding 8 mg/L, subject to stricter municipal pretreatment ordinances. Oily sludge, spent filter media, contaminated absorbents, and waste oil must be stored in sealed and segregated containers, transported using licensed hazardous waste carriers, and disposed of only by a waste treatment company approved under the Wastes Control Act, with detailed manifests retained for a minimum of three years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire safety inspection certificate and a completed firefighting systems inspection report from the local fire department under the Firefighting Systems Installation and Maintenance Act, including an operational self-defense firefighting and civil defense emergency plan approved by the local civil defense coordination committee. If the business site or any associated storage area contains petroleum or hazardous chemicals, secure a hazardous facilities fire protection authorization and a chemical accident prevention plan under the Hazardous Chemicals Management Act and the Chemicals Control Act. Register the workplace with the Ministry of Employment and Labor, conduct a workplace risk assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and appoint a workplace safety and health manager if the number of workers meets the statutory threshold. All occupational safety and health management plans, training records, emergency drills, and personal protective equipment logs must be maintained at the registered office and made available for inspection by labor authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic tax portal: HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, the Yuhan Hoesa must file an Application for Business Registration with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its registered head office within 20 days from the commencement of business, attaching its corporate formation documents such as the articles of incorporation, certificate of capital contribution, and identification of the representative director. The NTS then issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions simultaneously as the corporate Tax Identification Number and the VAT registration number, and the electronic business registration certificate is retrievable through the HomeTax portal. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic place of business that nevertheless incurs mandatory Korean VAT obligations in respect of cross-border supplies or imported transactions, the entity must appoint a tax representative, file a simplified VAT registration application with the NTS through HomeTax before commencing taxable activity, and obtain a simplified business registration number for VAT purposes. Because the Yuhan Hoesa is a domestically incorporated Korean limited company, the standard domestic BRN registration route is the governing procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic Korean limited liability company taxed at the corporate level on its worldwide income; pass-through treatment is not available; territorial scope = worldwide income with foreign tax credit relief; Tax-Exempt Zone = not applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None: Korean law has no check-the-box or pass-through classification election. Available elective regimes include the Consolidated Tax Filing Regime under the Corporate Tax Act for 100 percent owned domestic subsidiaries and the tax-neutral merger carryover election. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, effective 1 January 2020, apply mandatorily and carry no discretionary opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration exemption threshold exists in Korea; every business operator engaged in taxable supplies of goods or services must register with the NTS and obtain a Business Registration Number. An annual taxable turnover of KRW 80 million in the preceding calendar year is the statutory cutoff under the VAT Act between the general taxable person regime and the simplified taxable person regime, but it is a compliance classification threshold and not a registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea requires VAT-registered general taxable persons to issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax electronic invoice system and to transmit the e-invoice issuance data to the NTS no later than the day following invoice issuance. Machine-to-machine submission is enabled by NTS Open API and accredited ERP/accounting integrations using accredited digital certificates and electronic seals. Korea does not operate a real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) pre-clearance portal or an anti-fraud digital stamping regime; instead the NTS applies post-transaction e-invoice reporting supplemented by automated cross-matching between e-invoice data, customs export declarations, import records, and VAT refund validation algorithms.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, zero-rating is available for goods physically exported out of the Korean customs territory, including marine fuel oil and refined petroleum distillates that are laden on board a vessel departing from a Korean port for an international destination, as well as bunkering supplies to ships engaged exclusively in international voyages. Zero-rating also extends to foreign-exchange-earning services supplied to non-resident counterparties, such as oil brokerage and commission services for cross-border physical fuel trades, provided the recipient is a non-resident, the service is performed in the context of exports or foreign trade, and the invoice is issued in foreign currency or evidence of foreign-exchange earning is maintained. The Yuhan Hoesa must demonstrate through the statutory documentation bundle that title and beneficial ownership passed to the foreign buyer, that the goods departed the Korean customs territory under a valid export declaration, and that the sales proceeds were repatriated to Korea in foreign currency within the statutory deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certificate of Export Declaration (export clearance certificate) issued by the Korea Customs Service
Ocean Bill of Lading or Multimodal Transport Bill of Lading evidencing export shipment
Commercial invoice and packing list for the exported fuel shipment
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice (VAT e-invoice stated at 0 percent)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Bunker Delivery Note or marine fuel delivery receipt for fuel loaded on international-bound vessels
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Korea Customs Service and the NTS cross-verify e-invoice data against export declarations, vessel loading records, Bill of Lading duplicates, port records, bunker delivery receipts, and bank foreign exchange ledgers. If a zero-rated export claim is found to be unsubstantiated, false, or if the export proceeds are not repatriated in foreign currency within the statutory 180-day deadline, the NTS retroactively claws back the previously refunded VAT, imposes 10 percent VAT on the supply, assesses understatement penalty tax of 10 to 40 percent of the tax evaded or a 20 percent non-filing penalty when applicable, adds daily overdue interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and may refer the case for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, which carries imprisonment of up to three years and/or fines of up to three times the amount of tax evaded for fraudulent export zero-rating schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (the central bank of the Republic of Korea), jointly administering the foreign exchange regime with the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the network of registered Foreign Exchange Banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, administered by the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The current account is broadly convertible: payments for imports, trade-related services, and profit remittances are permitted through a registered Foreign Exchange Bank without individual licensing, subject to documentary verification and the filing of transaction reports. The capital account operates on a negative-list prior-declaration framework; foreign direct investments, cross-border loans, and securities purchases require a declaration or approval from the Foreign Exchange Bank or the Bank of Korea, with FDI additionally reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to obtain a certificate of registration and capital verification. There is no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio for export proceeds; Korean-resident enterprises may retain USD or other foreign currency in Foreign Exchange Bank accounts and forward-sell only against real underlying trade exposure. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal but real: dividends and branch profits can be remitted after the resolution of the shareholders' meeting, evidence of corporate tax withholding at the applicable 20-22 percent dividend withholding tax subject to treaty relief, and the submission of the Form 26-25 withholding tax payment certificate. Banks retain discretion to require additional FATCA and CRS self-certifications and economic substance documentation before allowing frequent large-value dividend or loan repayments to non-resident treasury centers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 8 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be received domestically within six months from the date the export declaration is accepted; the deadline can be extended by up to six additional months upon application to the responsible Foreign Exchange Bank, for a maximum of one year total. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may hold the foreign currency indefinitely in foreign currency deposit accounts, but any conversion into KRW or derivative hedging must be executed through the reporting bank and supported by the original export contract, the UNIPASS customs export declaration, and the trade settlement evidence. Failure to meet the collection deadline triggers an administrative fine and a compliance audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI capital verification and Basic Operational KRW/USD Current Account
Basic Operational KRW/USD Current Account with Commodity Trade Finance Desk
Basic Operational KRW/USD Current Account and Standby Letter of Credit Fronting Facility
Operational KRW/USD Current Account with Independent Energy-Sector Approval Committee

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary treasury rail for this high-risk energy-commodity licence. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act restrict the operation of foreign exchange services, deposit-taking, and trade settlement to banks licensed or registered with the Financial Services Commission as Foreign Exchange Banks. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex do not hold a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank licence and therefore cannot legally provide a dedicated Korean-designated collection account for an unregistered domestic physical petroleum trader; using them as the main settlement rail would breach the Foreign Exchange Bank reporting obligation and trigger automatic AML declines. Their maximum permitted utility is as an ancillary FX card or employee travel card; all principal collections and disbursements must be cleared through a tier-1 licensed Korean bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a high-risk special-license energy commodity entity under ISIC 4661 covering wholesale of crude oil and refined products, the statutory director and every ultimate beneficial owner holding 25 percent or more of the equity must appear physically at a domestic branch for the initial face-to-face KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by tier-1 Korean banks for this risk tier. A non-resident director may instead execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing a Korean resident director, chief financial officer, or local attorney-in-fact who attends the in-branch interview bearing the original passports, certified corporate documents, and the power of attorney verified by the Korean consulate or apostille authority. The appointed account signatory must also complete a separate in-person identity verification, and the bank will conduct a site visit of the registered business premises before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO and foreign directors create an opaque multi-jurisdiction ownership chain over a Korean LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of the Yuhan Hoesa articles of incorporation and the Korean Business Registration Certificate; notarized and apostilled shareholder ledger reflecting the Korean statutory ownership register translated into English, showing the full chain to the natural-person UBO; valid passports and alien registration cards of all directors and UBOs; proof of residential address provided by a utility bill dated within the last six months; tax residence certificates for each foreign shareholder; and FATCA Form W-8BEN-E plus CRS self-certifications filed with the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account purpose classification as a statutory-license petroleum wholesale broker without visible trading substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid registration certificate for the petroleum distribution business, being the petroleum refining, import, export, or wholesale license issued by the competent Korean city or provincial government; import and export trader registration under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act; fire safety permit for hazardous liquid handling; marine fuel bunker supply agreements with a licensed oil terminal operator; and the latest environmental and storage compliance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value SWIFT MT103 wire traffic and Standby Letter of Credit drawdown patterns inconsistent with the stated marine fuel brokerage business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original master sale and purchase contracts for crude oil or maritime distillates identifying counterparty, Incoterms, product specifications, quantity, and payment terms; shipment records including bills of lading, cargo manifests, and port receipts; a 12-to-24-month trade reconciliation and order history report; counterparty KYC packs and bank reference letters; an internal AML and sanctions-screening policy; IMO vessel screening for UN, OFAC, and EU sanctions; end-user declarations and attestation letters confirming no dealings with sanctioned states or entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital concentration risk showing a fast dividend or loan repayment to the non-resident parent shortly after the FDI capital injection in a quick-out pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Registration Certificate issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the bank's FDI declaration filing; board minutes and shareholders' resolutions authorizing the capital injection and the subsequent dividend distribution; the paid-in capital deposit certificate issued by the Foreign Exchange Bank; audited financial statements under Korean GAAP or IFRS demonstrating that the injected capital was deployed in genuine trade operations; the corporate tax withholding payment receipt on Form 26-25; and, for treaty-reduced withholding, the applicable Korea tax treaty residency certificate and the corresponding Form 26-25 filing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder must file a prior foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act at the receiving Foreign Exchange Bank or through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, also known as KOTRA, before the remittance; the bank then issues the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. Inbound equity arrives via SWIFT MT103 to the bank's dedicated FDI receivables account in the investor's name, with the remittance reference carrying the FDI report notification number and the stated purpose of inbound equity investment. The bank performs paid-in capital verification and issues a capital deposit certificate; the funds are then released into the operational KRW/USD account. If the funding is instead a shareholder loan from the foreign parent, a separate loan borrowing declaration must be filed and the proceeds converted to KRW only at the real-demand rate through the Foreign Exchange Bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Crude oil and refined product trade settlements should be executed through four clearing rails: direct SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers against the supplier's final invoice, the underlying sale and purchase contract, and the customs export declaration, with the remittance application citing the statutory trade purpose code; commercial documentary letters of credit, whether sight or usance, issued by the Korean home bank and advised or confirmed by the beneficiary's bank, payable via the SWIFT network; standby letters of credit deployed as a performance or payment guarantee rather than as the primary settlement instrument; and documentary collections, being D/P at sight or D/A with tenor, for matured open-account relationships. Every outbound disbursement requires the remittance application, the trade contract or letter of credit terms, the bill of lading or shipping evidence, and the Foreign Exchange Bank transaction declaration for amounts exceeding statutory thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/KRW forward outright contracts executed through a licensed Foreign Exchange Bank under the real-demand principle, supported by the underlying import purchase contract and the customs import declaration for the matching trade tenor

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for non-resident counterparties in the offshore USD/KRW market, or onshore as a complement only when the bank has approved the inherent risk limit and the petroleum trade exposure is documented
Cross-currency swaps (USD/KRW CCS) and cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for term mismatches between the KRW operational liquidity and USD trade payables or SBLC reimbursement obligations

Plain vanilla FX options, being call or put, with the premium paid in KRW, allowed strictly as a hedge against KRW appreciation or volatility on forecasted marine fuel oil and distillate disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular general meeting and shareholder/member approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The members/shareholders acting in general meeting; no public authority filing unless the company is externally audited or otherwise subject to public disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, on or before March 31. Court extension is available only for force majeure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare or present financial statements are subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act and may be jointly and severally liable for damages; persistent failure to hold an annual meeting can trigger court-ordered dissolution at the request of shareholders or creditors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit engagement and submission of independent auditor's report under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), with a copy to the National Tax Service where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The auditor must deliver the report before the annual general meeting and the report must be submitted to FSC/FSS within the statutory period; for a calendar-year audited Yuhan Hoesa this is normally completed by March 31 and in all cases before the corporate tax return deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to submit an audit report exposes the company to administrative fines; an auditor who knowingly issues a false audit report is subject to imprisonment up to 3 years or a criminal fine up to KRW 50,000,000; the company may also suffer tax return penalties for unsupported financial information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and payment, including related-party international transaction schedules and petroleum wholesale trading schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; by March 31 for a December 31 year-end. One additional month to April 30 is available when the return is prepared by a certified tax agent or when foreign-related transactions require extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of payable corporate tax; underreporting or omission triggers an additional tax of 10% of the underreported amount, or 40% for fraudulent or grossly negligent concealment; unpaid corporate tax accrues statutory late-payment interest at approximately 0.03% per day until settlement; NTS may seize accounts, attach receivables, cancel the business registration, and enforce compulsory collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Si/Gun/Gu local government tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory deadline as the corporate income tax return and payment; within 3 months after fiscal year-end, or within 4 months with an approved corporate tax extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underreporting triggers local income tax additional taxes of up to 20% of the deficient tax; late payment accrues daily overdue interest; prolonged delinquency permits local authorities to seize and publicly auction company assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax preliminary and final returns for marine fuel oil and refined distillate brokerage supplies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four returns per fiscal year: preliminary returns by April 25 and October 25; final semi-annual returns by July 25 and January 25.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The VAT Act imposes delinquent additional taxes on omitted or unpaid output VAT plus late-payment interest; false electronic tax invoices also attract penalties equal to 2% of supply value per invoice, and tax evasion is subject to criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly payroll and nonresident withholding tax remittance statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The 10th day of the following month for withholding of employee income tax and nonresident payments.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding taxes not remitted by the 10th day accrue statutory overdue interest until paid; the NTS may collect directly from company assets and responsible officers may be personally liable under the National Tax Collection Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested company annual status report and UBO confirmation report where non-resident shareholding exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the receiving domestic bank or Korean Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report by March 31 following the reporting calendar year; any transfer of shares changing foreign investment status must be reported within 30 days from the date of transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the foreign investment status report may suspend foreign-invested company benefits and attract administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; un-reported transfers also constitute a compliance defect for the registered agent and may result in registry correction orders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 4 of Korea's Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa must be independently audited by a certified public accountant if its total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end are KRW 12,000,000,000 or more, approximately USD 8,500,000. Mandatory audit also applies if the company is listed, is a public-interest company, is designated by the Financial Services Commission, or is a financial company. Turnover and headcount are not independent statutory audit triggers; however, the FSC may designate an audit for high-revenue marine fuel-oil trading companies where public-interest risk, turnover scale, employee count, and counterparty exposure warrant independent certified review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) applies to listed companies and FSC-designated public-interest companies; other Yuhan Hoesa entities may apply K-GAAP (Korean GAAP) as endorsed by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; simplified accounting standards may apply to small and medium companies not subject to statutory external audit. Accrual accounting, substance-over-form, consistency, and true-and-fair-view presentation are mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a standalone public UBO annual return for a private Yuhan Hoesa. However, under the Financial Transaction Reports Act and FSC customer due diligence rules, the company must identify and verify any natural person owning 25% or more of equity or ultimately controlling the entity at bank onboarding and before high-risk oil-trading wire transactions. If a non-resident shareholding is present, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires any transfer changing foreign investment status to be reported to the receiving bank or MOTIE within 30 days, plus an annual foreign-invested company status report by March 31. The register of members must be updated on the close of every transfer. There is no separate annual UBO filing with the court registry unless a corporate governance event requires court registration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 3,000 per year in Seoul and other major commercial centers; USD 400 - USD 1,500 outside major metropolitan areas.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 40,000 per year for a mid-sized Yuhan Hoesa in marine fuel-oil wholesale brokerage under K-GAAP without group consolidation; USD 15,000 - USD 60,000 additional for K-IFRS, group consolidation, or FSC-designated public-interest audit engagement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (maximum national corporate income tax rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; lower progressive brackets: 9%, 19%, and 21%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A 10% local income tax surcharge applies, making the aggregate effective top rate 26.4%. Korea does not grant routine offshore tax holidays; however, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act allows a 50% corporate tax exemption for 3-5 years to qualified advanced-technology foreign-invested enterprises in free trade zones. An R&D super-deduction (generally up to 25%) and a preferential patent box-style rate of 5% for qualifying patent income are available; energy brokerages do not qualify unless performing eligible R&D.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return for Domestic Corporations (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Payable Calculation Statement) / National Tax Service Hometax electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional tax payments are due during the fiscal year for entities that reported taxable income in the prior year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 March of the following year; if the deadline falls on a holiday, the next business day

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, corporate registration number, representative's resident registration number, fiscal year, industry code and registered address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify every non-resident shareholder by country of residence and ownership percentage. Where a foreign corporation is the ultimate owner, provide the foreign corporate number and Korean resident tax representative. Failure to disclose the beneficial owner may suspend treaty withholding relief and trigger a beneficial ownership audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, commissions, brokerage fees and other consideration derived from wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and refined petroleum products
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross commissions earned on bunker sale brokerage as Korean-source business income. Costs and counterparty disbursements cannot be netted against gross income. A foreign-owned Korean entity must not recharacterize brokerage commissions as non-taxable cost reimbursements unless there is contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and corrections for non-deductible related-party payments, excessive intercompany fees, interest, royalties, and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions in attached Schedule TP. For transactions with foreign affiliates whose aggregate gross amount equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion, Local File and Master File must be submitted before the filing deadline. The taxpayer must demonstrate that brokerage fees, ocean-freight reimbursements, and credit charges meet the arm's-length standard; otherwise the examiner will impute income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base calculated after statutory loss carryforward, non-taxable income, and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Korean-entity operating losses may be deducted, and the deduction period is limited to 10 years. Losses may be deducted up to the full statutory tax base but cannot be used by foreign shareholders to offset their home-country income. A Yuhan Hoesa that switches from marketing-only to full trading risk can expect scrutiny of the loss history.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate tax computed from taxable income using the 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% progressive brackets, before local income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the tax on the exact progressive segment, then add 10% local income tax surcharge. A non-resident dividend distribution is not a deductible expense in Korea. Any tax credit for foreign taxes withheld abroad is available only under a DTA and after filing Form for tax credit; unsubstantiated credits are rejected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Late filing surcharges, understatement penalties, late payment interest, and prior-year adjustment items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors signing the return should quantify all related-party high-risk categories. If the NTS subsequently makes a TP adjustment, additional tax is assessed from the original due date and the 10% local income tax applies; personal asset exposure follows if the entity cannot pay.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: an additional tax equal to 20% of the final corporate income tax payable if no return is filed; late payment: a daily surcharge of 0.022% of the unpaid amount from the statutory deadline to payment date; negligent understatement: 10% of the understated tax; fraudulent understatement: 40% of the understated tax; non-submission of transfer pricing documentation: up to KRW 10 million or more, plus denial of the underlying deduction. Persistent non-compliance subjects the Representative Director and tax representative to personal collection and prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge (10% of the national tax), giving a statutory aggregate of 22% on gross Korean-source dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; treaty-reduced rates may apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain from the competent tax authority of its residence a current-year Tax Residency Certificate (TRC); complete the Korean National Tax Service application for treaty reduction/exemption (Application for Income Tax Reduction or Exemption by Tax Treaty); provide the Korean paying entity with a beneficial ownership certificate showing the minimum shareholding period (typically at least 365 days if the DTA requires it) and the actual entitlement to dividends; and, where withholding was taken at the statutory rate, file a refund claim with the Hometax foreign tax desk. Principal purpose/general anti-abuse and substance tests apply, and a shell company with no economic activity in the treaty country will be denied relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for cross-border interest and royalties are also 20% national plus 2% local surcharge = 22% aggregate. Under relevant OECD-based Korean DTAs the treaty ceiling is usually 10% for interest and 10%-15% for royalties, with possible 0% for certain state-owned financial institutions; all treaty benefits require TRC, arm's-length interest/royalty and beneficial ownership certification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation/submission is triggered when the aggregate gross amount of cross-border related-party transactions in a fiscal year is KRW 10 billion or more. In addition, a Country-by-Country Report is required for Korean ultimate parent entities or Korean constituent entities of MNE groups with consolidated revenue of KRW 100 billion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea enforces economic substance through the Corporate Tax Act, the International Tax Adjustment Act, the substance-over-form doctrine, and the Beneficial Ownership rule in the tax treaties. An energy-trading Yuhan Hoesa must have real premises, qualified staff, board decision-making at Korean board meetings, risk-bearing capital, and active contract negotiation, voyage-risk management, credit control, and payment-settlement functions in Korea. It must not be a mere booking center for a foreign principal; the Korean entity's OECD-compliant Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) have to match the profit allocation. The CIGA standard is now applied by the Korean National Tax Service when recharacterizing commission income as a taxable permanent establishment, denying DTA benefits, or applying controlled foreign corporation (CFC) rules to passive income parked abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Fabricated Bunker Supply and Brokerage Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or booking false invoices for marine fuel oil purchases, artificially inflating freight and customs costs, creating sham intermediary commissions to related shell companies, under-reporting brokerage fees from bunker resales, or using cash and unaccounted SWIFT wire transfers to conceal taxable income of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and Article 121 of the Corporate Tax Act: imprisonment up to 5 years, a criminal fine up to three times the evaded tax, plus civil penalties of 10%-40% of the understated tax, daily late-payment surcharges, and recovery of the full tax, local surtax and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Representative Director and any director who participated in the false filing can be personally named as secondary taxpayers; the National Tax Service may levy on personal bank accounts, real estate, and vehicles, block director departure through a foreign-travel blacklist, and refer the director to criminal prosecution. Under Korean Commercial Act Article 401, directors who intentionally or negligently cause harm to third parties are jointly and severally liable for damages, effectively piercing the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Paper-Only Intermediary Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking all economic profit in a zero-tax foreign subsidiary while the Korean entity performs no substantive negotiation, logistics, credit, or risk functions; charging non-arm's-length service fees; failing to file Local/Master File by the deadline; or routing crude oil and refined products contracts through a treaty-shopping shell solely to obtain refunds and reduced withholding rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 4 and 18 of the International Tax Adjustment Act and the principal purpose rule, the National Tax Service adjusts taxable income to arm's-length levels, adds a TP documentation penalty, applies a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty, denies DTA protection, and assesses 24% national plus 2.4% local surtax on the adjusted profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false TP schedules face secondary liability for the adjusted tax and penalties; the corporate veil is pierced if the entity was formed as a sham; NTS can attach director assets and issue departure restrictions pending payment. Willful false TP documentation is treated as tax evasion and can result in incarceration of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions Evasion, Trade-Based Money Laundering and Cross-Border Payment Illegality
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling marine fuel oil or refined distillates to or through designated UN/OFAC- or Korea-designated sanctioned persons, vessels or jurisdictions, presenting forged certificates of origin or ownership, using standby letters of credit fraudulently, moving payments through shell banks or unlicensed money transmitters via SWIFT, or failing to report suspicious transactions in the high-risk energy commodity trading channel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (AML) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act: criminal imprisonment up to 5 years and criminal fines up to KRW 500 million or three times the laundered proceeds for each transaction; in addition, the Energy/ISIC license for wholesale fuel brokerage may be revoked and the customs duty/tax benefits forfeited, and tax deductions for illegal bribes or black-market payments are disallowed, generating additional corporate tax and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be directly prosecuted for money laundering and sanctions evasion, personally fined, and imprisoned; assets acquired from proceeds can be seized and confiscated. The director will be subject to a Korean departure ban, placed on the AML/blacklist, and disqualified as a fit-and-proper officer for any licensed financial or energy entity; the court may pierce the corporate veil where the Yuhan Hoesa is used as an instrumentality for crime and impose joint personal liability for the full tax, penalty, and third-party losses.
